title: Guntur Taluk — 1961 Census-era heritage and worship observations
source_scope: Guntur Taluk, Guntur District, Andhra Pradesh
method: Structured extraction from the Guntur Taluk Fairs and Festivals section. Place names and temple names follow the source as closely as possible; uncertain OCR or unreadable material is flagged rather than guessed.

localities.name: Amaravathi
history: The source connects Amaravathi and Dharanikota and records the older name forms of Dharanikota, including Dhanyakataka and related variants.
It describes inscriptions in the area, including a Kota-period inscription in Saka 1104 referring to Amareswara and a later inscription in Saka 1283 stating that Amareswara was reinstalled.
It records later patronage associated with Sri Krishna Devaraya and Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Naidu.
The source describes the Amaravathi stupa, Buddhist antiquities and the later development of Amareswara worship.
festivals: Mahasivaratri / Sri Amareswaraswamy festival — 10 days from Magha Bahula Dasami to Suddha Chavithi, according to the source.
localities.notes: The source contains extensive legends from the Skandapurana and Sthalapurana. These are retained as traditional narratives, not modern historical verification.

localities.name: Ananthavaram
worship_sites: Sri Venkateswaraswamy temple, with stone image on a hillock
festivals: Sri Venkateswaraswamy worship on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturdays from Magham to Vaisakham; offerings include coconuts, milk, butter, rice and fruits.
Marriages, thread-marriages and tonsure ceremonies are recorded at the temple.
sources_in_source: Sri N. Jaggaiah, Teacher, Ananthavaram
Sri Vaddemanu Malligaiah, Teacher, Ananthavaram

localities.name: Vaikunthapuram
history: The source says the village was formerly called Buddha-viramam and preserves an oral story about the name change.
It records a tradition that Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Naidu constructed the Venkateswara temple after consulting pandits and invited sixty Vaishnava Brahmin families for regular worship.
festivals: Venkateswaraswamy Kalyanam — 5 days during Sri Rama Navami.
Venkateswaraswamy Aradhana — one day on Ashada Suddha Ekadasi.
localities.notes: The source also reports Buddhist-age marble images found on Bhairava Dibba; this is an archaeological observation in the historical source and should be separately verified.

localities.name: Velagapudi
worship_sites: Village sacred abodes of Poleramma, Perantalu, Pothuraju, Mahalakshmamma, Ankamma, Maddi Ramamma, Maremma and Madar Saheb
history: The source explains the locality name as connected with numerous wood-apple gardens; it gives the vernacular element 'Velaga' as wood-apple.
festivals: Sri Rama Kalyanam — 5 days from Chaitra Suddha Navami.
Daily pujas to Someswaraswamy.
Anjaneyaswamy receives naivedyam in Kartikam and on Saturdays.
Devotees fast and perform abhishekams to Veera Malleswaraswamy.

localities.name: Sitanagaram hamlet of Tadepalle
worship_sites: Sri Lakshmi Narasimhaswamy (associated with the Theppothsavam)
festivals: Sri Lakshmi Narasimhaswamy Theppothsavam (boat festival) — one day in Magham.
localities.notes: The source passage specifically records the boat festival; it does not provide enough detail here to reconstruct a complete temple profile.

localities.name: Gundemeda
history: The source says Eastern Chalukya inscriptions mention Kota chiefs ruling Kandravadi with Ganderu as capital and states that Gundemeda formed part of Kandravadi.
festivals: Sri Sivakesavula Uthsavam — 2 days on Asviyuja Suddha Navami and Dasami; the source calls it an ancient festival of local significance.
sources_in_source: Sri S. Hanumantha Rao, Gundemada

localities.name: Nuthakki
festivals: Venugopalaswamy Uthsavam — 2 days in Magham; the source records about 1,000 participating devotees.
sources_in_source: Statement of fairs and festivals furnished by Superintendent of Police, Guntur

localities.name: Pedavadlapudi

localities.name: Ippatam
history: The source records a former fort on a mound and says the name Vippatam gradually changed into Ippatam, connecting it with the vernacular vippukunta meaning to break open or split.
festivals: Bhramaramba Malleswaraswamy Uthsavam — 9 days from Asviyuja Suddha Vidiya to Dasami; the source calls it ancient but locally significant.
Balija mutt Aradhana — Kartika Suddha Purnima.
Mollempudi Sri Venugopalaswamy Kalyanam — one day on Margasira Suddha Purnima; Paruveta Uthsavam on Asviyuja Suddha Dasami.

localities.name: Mangalagiri
worship_sites: Panakala Lakshmi Narasimhaswamy temple on the hill
Sri Venkateswaraswamy temple midway on the hill steps
Sri Lakshmi temple behind the Panakala shrine
Sri Rama temple with Sita and Lakshmana
history: The source translates Mangalagiri as 'the auspicious hill'.
A stone pillar near the foot of the steps carries Telugu inscriptions dated A.D. 1520 and records grants; the text connects it with the capture of Kondavidu in 1515.
Another inscription near the Garudalvar shrine records grants during the reign of Sadasiva Raya in A.D. 1558.
The source records later construction of the large eastern gopuram and associates its present form with Vasireddy Venkatadri Naidu, while also preserving other attributions as competing accounts.
The source describes the Panakala Narasimha legends and the traditional association of panakam (jaggery water) with the deity.
architecture: Eastern gopuram of the lower Lakshmi Narasimha temple is described as about 125 feet high with 11 storeys.
The source records an ancient temple car with wood carvings depicting scenes from the Mahabharata, Bhagavata and Ramayana.
festivals: Panakala Lakshmi Narasimhaswamy Brahmothsavam — described as an important annual festival; the source records an 11-day celebration in its period.
Srirama Navami, Hanuman Jayanthi, Narasimha Jayanthi and Vaikuntha Ekadasi are also recorded as major observances.
A fair is described as accompanying the Brahmothsavam.

localities.name: Pedaparimi
worship_sites: Malleswaraswamy temple with Siva linga and Bhramaramba
Venugopala shrine associated with the recorded Kalyanam
history: The source gives the former name Vathsavayipalem and associates it with Vathsavayi rulers. It then describes a later settlement history and the adoption of the name Pedaparimi.
festivals: Sri Malleswara Bhramaramba Kalyanothsavam — 6 days from Kartika Bahula Dasami to Amavasya; the source calls it ancient and locally significant.
Sri Venugopala Rukmini Kalyanam — 6 days from Vaisakha Suddha Dasami to Purnima; the source calls it ancient and says it extended to nearby villages.
Sivaratri, Sankranti, Srirama Navami and Sri Krishna Jayanthi are also recorded.

localities.name: Ravela
worship_sites: Sri Veeranjaneyaswamy temple in Kamaiah Thopu
history: The source says the Veeranjaneyaswamy image originally belonged to a temple in neighbouring Thurlapadu. It states that after the village was deserted the temple fell into ruins and the image was exposed, then in 1937 the Seetharamanjaneya Society led by Subba Rao brought and installed the image at Ravela.
A mantapam was described as recently constructed by Sri Thalia Veera Reddy.
festivals: Srirama Navami — 3 days from Chaitra Suddha Navami to Ekadasi; described as an ancient local festival.
Jatara for Poleramma, Maha Lakshmamma and Ankamma — every 20 or 30 years or during famine/epidemics, according to the source.
Sri Venugopalaswamy Uthsavam — 3 days during Dasara; Pongallu offerings and procession are recorded.
sources_in_source: Sri R. Venkata Siva Sitharamarao, Village Karnam, Ravela

localities.name: Mandapadu
festivals: Srirama Navami — 2 days from Chaitra Suddha Navami and Dasami.
localities.notes: The visible passage records the festival but does not provide a named temple in the supplied section.

localities.name: Perecherla
festivals: Guru Sydula Urs — 3 days in Ramzan; local devotees are recorded as participating without distinction of caste or creed.
localities.notes: The locality name is readable on the map/index, but the narrative heading is lost in OCR on the supplied page. Do not infer a temple from this passage.

localities.name: Nidumukkala
history: The source says the village was under Vijayanagar Kings and the Reddys of Kondavidu and begins quoting the Krishna District Manual about an inscription of Krishna Raja.
localities.notes: The supplied PDF ends during the Nidumukkala entry, so its worship-site information is incomplete in this file.

data_policy.historical_observation: The 1961 source is preserved as a time-stamped historical snapshot, not as proof that every named shrine still exists in the same form today.
data_policy.traditional_claim: Legends, beliefs and oral explanations remain explicitly attributed to the source.
data_policy.current_match: A historical worship site will only be linked to a modern temple record after independent location/name verification.
data_policy.ocr_uncertainty: Where the scan or OCR is unclear, the record is flagged instead of silently correcting the source.
